milestone.about: Entrustment-based discussion portion of Mini-CEX and EBD: milestone descriptors. Value 0.5 = Not Yet Achieved Level 1; 1.0-5.0 in half steps shown as 1-9. Descriptors exist for 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 (milestone levels 1-5) and differ per competency; see "descriptors" on each question. Medical knowledge and clinical reasoning are compulsory.

descriptions.1: The trainee has permission only to be present but not to enact this EPA.
descriptions.2: Supervisor needs to be present in the SAME room as the resident at all times. Pro-active supervision is required for all / most clinical activities.
descriptions.3: Supervisor need not be in the same room as resident but remains within the healthcare facility, contactable and ready to respond within minutes to any call for help by the resident e.g., the supervisor having a meal break while the resident remains alone to care for the patient.
descriptions.4: Supervisor is not present in healthcare facility but remains contactable via phone call to provide advice and supervision remotely.
descriptions.5: The trainee is able to guide others in this EPA.

EBD.medhubName: (2023) EBD EPA (n): (topic), e.g. "(2023) EBD EPA (5): (HeadNeck Trauma)"
introduction: This is a FORMATIVE assessment to be conducted by a faculty member who directly observed the trainee while co-managing the case.
The case can be chosen by the trainee in consultation with the faculty.
The faculty should conduct an Entrustment-Based Discussion (EbD) as soon as possible after the completion of the case.
After conducting the EbD, please document the trainee's discussion with faculty and reflections on the case.
Please grade the trainee on the 9-point scale based on descriptors below.
Please comment on what the trainee did well and can be improved upon.
Please also record the supervision level that you would theoretically entrust the trainee with for this particular EPA.

questions.label: Complexity of Case

sections.section: Please mark the areas for improvement based on OBSERVED PERFORMANCE of the resident.

options: Communication skills with patient/ next of kin

questions.label: Comments (if any of the areas of improvement are checked)
Please briefly describe what was discussed centered around at least 2 entrustment questions

sections.section: Based on the discussion, please assess the following

questions.label: Medical Knowledge

descriptors.1: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology / treatment of medical and surgical considerations and identifies medications used to treat common comorbidities
descriptors.3: Demonstrates knowledge of common medical / surgical disease / medications routinely used in anaesthestic care
descriptors.5: Demonstrates knowledge of complex medical / surgical disease / medication used in subspecialty anaesthesia
descriptors.7: Demonstrates knowledge of medical / surgical disease as it relates to full spectrum of patient's perioperative care / pharmacology in setting of complex comorbidities
descriptors.9: Demonstrates knowledge of uncommon, complex, atypical conditions as it applies to the full spectrum of patient's perioperative care / participates in research related to pharmacology / pathophysiology relevant to anaesthesia

questions.label: Clinical reasoning skills

descriptors.1: Organizes and accurately summarizes patient information and list types of clinical reasoning errors
descriptors.3: Integrates information to form basic differential diagnosis for common patient presentations / Identifies clinical reasoning errors with guidance
descriptors.5: Develops a thorough and prioritised differential diagnosis for common patient presentation and able to apply clinical reasoning principles to identify errors
descriptors.7: Develops prioritised differential diagnosis in complex patient presentations and notes peculiarities of case / continually self reappraises clinical reasoning
descriptors.9: Coaches others to develop prioritised differential diagnoses in complex patients and models how to recognise errors and reflect on own clinical reasoning

questions.label: Use of evidence based medicine

descriptors.1: Accesses and uses evidence in routine patient care
descriptors.3: Articulates clinical question and elicits patient preferences and to guide evidence based care
descriptors.5: Locates and applies best evidence based evidence integrated with patient preference to care of complex patients
descriptors.7: Appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide individualised care
descriptors.9: Coaches others to appraise and apply evidence based care and / or participates in development of guidelines

questions.label: Healthcare system awareness

descriptors.1: Identifies key components of the complex healthcare system that affects anaesthetic care and patient experience and factors impacting the cost of anaesthetic care
descriptors.3: Describes how components of a complex health care system interrelate and impact patient care and documents anaesthetic details to facilitate accurate billing
descriptors.5: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system and explains the impact of documentation on billing and reimbursement
descriptors.7: Manages various components of the complex healthcare system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition
descriptors.9: Advocates for or leads system change that enhances high-value, efficient and effective patient care and engages in external activities to advocate for cost effective care

rules: Only physician / core faculty may assess Mini-CEX, DOPS and EBD; senior residents do not assess EPAs.
EBD assessors must have co-managed the case.
Faculty and resident agree on the case. After the observed assessment the resident triggers the form to the assessor and fills in the case details first.
The same patient can be used for at most 2 EPA assessments, each on its own form.
Forms should be filled within 24 hours of being triggered; otherwise the assessor gets a reminder email.
Residents should complete the relevant Mini-CEX, DOPS and EBD for an EPA by the end of each clinical rotation.
Assessors with a conflict of interest (e.g. close relations) should not assess and should flag it to the programme.
At least 2 entrustment questions per assessment; the discussion must follow an actual case.
